subject: Polishing of Figures and log-log Scale

messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Polishing of Figures and log-log Scale
parts:
Dear All,
I find ggplot2 wonderful, but there are a few things I am still
struggling with.
I would like to be able to generate figures along the lines of those in
this preprint (most likely obtained with Grace), e.g. look at Figure 2

http://arxiv.org/pdf/1002.4109

In general I am very pleased with ggplot2 gray default layout, but
consider the code snippet at the end of the email.
There are a few remarks (intended as constructive criticism) I would
like to make (probably it all amounts to slight changes to the defaults).
(1) I find that the thinner white lines are a bit confusing. What values
would they stand for in this case? Can I fine-tune them?.
(2) Can I add just the axis ticks at e.g. 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80,
90 (and their multiples by powers of 10) in the plot? That would make it
more readable, especially when I am not plotting something this trivial.
(3) If I uncomment the line

#theme_set(theme_bw())

, then the plot looks considerably uglier and axis titles and text
overlap. If I comment back that line and re-run the script, then I do
not get the default gray theme. Why is that?


Any suggestion is welcome.
Many thanks

Lorenzo

P.S.: I am on ubuntu 9.10, amd64 architeture, Cairo and ggplot2
installed from sources in CRAN.

###########################################################################################
###########################################################################################
###########################################################################################

my_df <- cbind(as.data.frame(10^seq(5)),as.data.frame(10^seq(5)))

names(my_df) <- c("x","y")

my_ybreaks <- c(1e1,1e2,1e3,1e4,1e5)
my_xbreaks <- c(1e1,1e2,1e3,1e4,1e5)

#theme_set(theme_bw())

gpl <- ggplot(my_df,aes(x=x,y=y) )+
geom_line()+
ylab("Time")+
xlab("Some function")+
scale_x_continuous(trans="log10", limits=c(10,1e5), breaks=my_xbreaks)+
scale_y_continuous(trans="log10", limits=c(10,1e5), breaks=my_ybreaks)+
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size=35))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 35, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=30, colour="black",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=30, colour="black", hjust=1))

CairoPDF("log-log-plot.pdf")
print(gpl)
dev.off()

the middle value of two major grids? I guess you can fine-tune them
using minor_breaks from scale_continuous like what you did in your
code.

> (2) Can I add just the axis ticks at e.g.  20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90

> readable, especially when I am not plotting something this trivial.

scale_continuous? or if you don't need the grid lines, just remove all
of them and draw those you want with geom_vline.

> (3) If I uncomment the line
>
> #theme_set(theme_bw())
>
> , then the plot looks considerably uglier and axis titles and text overlap.
> If I comment back that line and re-run the script, then I do not get the
> default gray theme. Why is that?

because theme_grey and theme_bw have different default values (colour
is not the only difference), and your customized theme values (from
the opts(...)) are not compatible well with theme_bw.

Thanks for your reply. A potential improvement is given by the code
snippet at the end of the email. A question: it is easy to switch off
the minor grid lines, but what if I want to have the corresponding
(minor) axis ticks?
I found this old thread

http://tinyurl.com/y99j3wz

and it looks that it is (was?) impossible to achieve this.
Is it still so? Does anyone know a workaround?
Cheers

Lorenzo


###############################################################
###############################################################

library(Cairo)
library(ggplot2)

my_df <- cbind(as.data.frame(10^seq(5)),as.data.frame(10^seq(5)))
names(my_df) <- c("x","y")

theme_set(theme_gray())

mb <- rep(1:10, length(my_ybreaks))
mul <- floor(seq(length(mb))/10)+1
mul2 <- 10^mul

mb <- mb*mul2

gpl <- ggplot(my_df,aes(x=x,y=y) )+ # BaseThemeX90()+

geom_line()+
ylab("Time")+
xlab("Some function")+

scale_x_continuous(trans="log10", limits=c(10,1e5), breaks=my_xbreaks,
minor_breaks=mb,expand=c(0.05, 0))+
scale_y_continuous(trans="log10", limits=c(10,1e5), breaks=my_ybreaks,
minor_breaks=mb,expand=c(0.05, 0))+

opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size=35))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 35, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=30, colour="black",vjust=1))+

opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=30, colour="black", hjust=1))+
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_line(colour = "darkgrey",size=0.3),
panel.grid.minor =theme_line(colour="darkgrey", size=0.1))+
opts(panel.background = theme_rect())

CairoPDF("log-log-plot.pdf")
print(gpl)
dev.off()

#################################################
#################################################
#################################################

library(Cairo)
library(ggplot2)

my_df <- cbind(as.data.frame(10^seq(5)),as.data.frame(10^seq(5)))
names(my_df) <- c("x","y")

theme_set(theme_gray())

mb <- c(seq(10,100,by=10),seq(200,1000, by=100),
seq(2e3,1e4,by=1e3),seq(2e4,1e5,by=1e4))

my_sel <- seq(1,length(mb), by=9)

my_label2 <- rep("",length(mb))
my_label2[my_sel] <- expression(10^1 ,10^2,10^3,10^4,10^5)

gpl <- ggplot(my_df,aes(x=x,y=y) )+
geom_vline(xintercept = seq(0,5,by=1), col="white", size=1)+
geom_hline(yintercept = seq(0,5,by=1), col="white", size=1)+

geom_line()+
ylab("Time")+
xlab("Some function")+

scale_x_continuous(trans="log10", limits=c(10,1e5), breaks=mb,
label=my_label2)+
scale_y_continuous(trans="log10", limits=c(10,1e5), breaks=mb,
label=my_label2)+
opts(panel.grid.minor = theme_blank())+
opts(panel.grid.major = theme_blank())+

opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size=35))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 35, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=30, colour="black",vjust=1))+
